=== Pocket Smear ===

Pocket Smear is for exactly 3 players, seated as Player 1, Player 2 and Player 3. Seat order is 1, 2, 3, then back to 1.

DECK: 24 cards in three suits (Red, Blue, Green), each with ranks 1 to 8. Cards are shown as codes suit*10+rank (Red=1, Blue=2, Green=3), so 18 is Red 8 and 23 is Blue 3. Card points, used only for Game: rank 8 = 4, rank 7 = 3, rank 6 = 2, rank 5 = 1, all other ranks = 0.

STRUCTURE: The game is 9 deals of 4 tricks each, one trick per round (36 rounds). Player 1 deals deals 1, 4 and 7; Player 2 deals 2, 5 and 8; Player 3 deals 3, 6 and 9. Priority order for a deal is: the player after the dealer, then the next player, then the dealer. All scores start at 0.

DEAL: All 24 cards are shuffled and each player is dealt 4 private cards. The other 12 are set aside face down, unseen by anyone, for the whole deal. You see only your own hand.

BID: Everyone answers at the same moment with one answer of two parts: PASS or a whole number from 2 to 6, and one suit that is in your own hand. A suit must be named even when passing (for example '4 Blue' or 'PASS Red'). Every player's amount (or PASS) is then revealed. The highest number wins: that player becomes the pitcher, the number becomes the contract and their named suit becomes trump. A tie goes to the tied player who comes first in priority order. If all three pass, the dealer becomes the pitcher with contract 2, and trump is the suit the dealer named. The pitcher, contract and trump are announced; the suits named by the other two players are never revealed.

TRICKS: Three cards are played one at a time, starting with the leader and continuing in seat order. In the first trick of a deal the pitcher leads and must lead a trump (they always hold one). In later tricks the winner of the previous trick leads any card. Each later player must play a card of the led suit if they hold one, but may instead play a trump even if they hold the led suit; a player holding no card of the led suit may play any card. You are only offered legal cards. The trick goes to the highest-ranked trump played; if no trump was played, it goes to the highest-ranked card of the led suit. All played cards are visible to everyone, and the three cards go into the trick winner's captured pile.

DEAL SCORING (after the 4th trick; only cards played this deal count): HIGH, 1 point, to the player who captured the highest-ranked trump played. LOW, 1 point, to the player who captured the lowest-ranked trump played (this may be the same card as High). GAME, 1 point, to the player whose captured pile has the most card points; if two or more players tie for most, nobody scores Game. THREE, 3 points, to the player who captured the trump of rank 3; if it was not dealt, nobody scores it. Each player's deal points are the sum of the categories they won, from 0 to 6. Each of the two non-pitchers adds their deal points to their score. If the pitcher's deal points are at least the contract, the pitcher adds their deal points to their score. Otherwise the pitcher is SET: the pitcher subtracts the contract from their score and does not add their deal points. Scores may go negative. Captured piles are then cleared and the next deal begins.

COMMUNICATION: There is no table talk. Players communicate only through bids and played cards.

END: After the 9th deal is scored, the game ends. The highest total score wins; players tied for the highest total share the result (a draw).

records.raw:
Green is my best trump suit. I hold Green 3, worth 3 points, and Green 2, which is likely Low. But both are low cards, and the other players probably hold higher Greens that could capture them, so bidding high risks being set.

As dealer I lose any tie. That makes "PASS Green" play the same as "2 Green": if the others both pass, I become pitcher anyway at contract 2 with Green as trump. If either of them bids, they win either way.

PASS Green

=== Pocket Smear ===

Pocket Smear is for exactly 3 players, seated as Player 1, Player 2 and Player 3. Seat order is 1, 2, 3, then back to 1.

DECK: 24 cards in three suits (Red, Blue, Green), each with ranks 1 to 8. Cards are shown as codes suit*10+rank (Red=1, Blue=2, Green=3), so 18 is Red 8 and 23 is Blue 3. Card points, used only for Game: rank 8 = 4, rank 7 = 3, rank 6 = 2, rank 5 = 1, all other ranks = 0.

STRUCTURE: The game is 9 deals of 4 tricks each, one trick per round (36 rounds). Player 1 deals deals 1, 4 and 7; Player 2 deals 2, 5 and 8; Player 3 deals 3, 6 and 9. Priority order for a deal is: the player after the dealer, then the next player, then the dealer. All scores start at 0.

DEAL: All 24 cards are shuffled and each player is dealt 4 private cards. The other 12 are set aside face down, unseen by anyone, for the whole deal. You see only your own hand.

BID: Everyone answers at the same moment with one answer of two parts: PASS or a whole number from 2 to 6, and one suit that is in your own hand. A suit must be named even when passing (for example '4 Blue' or 'PASS Red'). Every player's amount (or PASS) is then revealed. The highest number wins: that player becomes the pitcher, the number becomes the contract and their named suit becomes trump. A tie goes to the tied player who comes first in priority order. If all three pass, the dealer becomes the pitcher with contract 2, and trump is the suit the dealer named. The pitcher, contract and trump are announced; the suits named by the other two players are never revealed.

TRICKS: Three cards are played one at a time, starting with the leader and continuing in seat order. In the first trick of a deal the pitcher leads and must lead a trump (they always hold one). In later tricks the winner of the previous trick leads any card. Each later player must play a card of the led suit if they hold one, but may instead play a trump even if they hold the led suit; a player holding no card of the led suit may play any card. You are only offered legal cards. The trick goes to the highest-ranked trump played; if no trump was played, it goes to the highest-ranked card of the led suit. All played cards are visible to everyone, and the three cards go into the trick winner's captured pile.

DEAL SCORING (after the 4th trick; only cards played this deal count): HIGH, 1 point, to the player who captured the highest-ranked trump played. LOW, 1 point, to the player who captured the lowest-ranked trump played (this may be the same card as High). GAME, 1 point, to the player whose captured pile has the most card points; if two or more players tie for most, nobody scores Game. THREE, 3 points, to the player who captured the trump of rank 3; if it was not dealt, nobody scores it. Each player's deal points are the sum of the categories they won, from 0 to 6. Each of the two non-pitchers adds their deal points to their score. If the pitcher's deal points are at least the contract, the pitcher adds their deal points to their score. Otherwise the pitcher is SET: the pitcher subtracts the contract from their score and does not add their deal points. Scores may go negative. Captured piles are then cleared and the next deal begins.

COMMUNICATION: There is no table talk. Players communicate only through bids and played cards.

END: After the 9th deal is scored, the game ends. The highest total score wins; players tied for the highest total share the result (a draw).

Players: 3. Seats are numbered 1 to 3.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

=== Pocket Smear ===

Pocket Smear is for exactly 3 players, seated as Player 1, Player 2 and Player 3. Seat order is 1, 2, 3, then back to 1.

DECK: 24 cards in three suits (Red, Blue, Green), each with ranks 1 to 8. Cards are shown as codes suit*10+rank (Red=1, Blue=2, Green=3), so 18 is Red 8 and 23 is Blue 3. Card points, used only for Game: rank 8 = 4, rank 7 = 3, rank 6 = 2, rank 5 = 1, all other ranks = 0.

STRUCTURE: The game is 9 deals of 4 tricks each, one trick per round (36 rounds). Player 1 deals deals 1, 4 and 7; Player 2 deals 2, 5 and 8; Player 3 deals 3, 6 and 9. Priority order for a deal is: the player after the dealer, then the next player, then the dealer. All scores start at 0.

DEAL: All 24 cards are shuffled and each player is dealt 4 private cards. The other 12 are set aside face down, unseen by anyone, for the whole deal. You see only your own hand.

BID: Everyone answers at the same moment with one answer of two parts: PASS or a whole number from 2 to 6, and one suit that is in your own hand. A suit must be named even when passing (for example '4 Blue' or 'PASS Red'). Every player's amount (or PASS) is then revealed. The highest number wins: that player becomes the pitcher, the number becomes the contract and their named suit becomes trump. A tie goes to the tied player who comes first in priority order. If all three pass, the dealer becomes the pitcher with contract 2, and trump is the suit the dealer named. The pitcher, contract and trump are announced; the suits named by the other two players are never revealed.

TRICKS: Three cards are played one at a time, starting with the leader and continuing in seat order. In the first trick of a deal the pitcher leads and must lead a trump (they always hold one). In later tricks the winner of the previous trick leads any card. Each later player must play a card of the led suit if they hold one, but may instead play a trump even if they hold the led suit; a player holding no card of the led suit may play any card. You are only offered legal cards. The trick goes to the highest-ranked trump played; if no trump was played, it goes to the highest-ranked card of the led suit. All played cards are visible to everyone, and the three cards go into the trick winner's captured pile.

DEAL SCORING (after the 4th trick; only cards played this deal count): HIGH, 1 point, to the player who captured the highest-ranked trump played. LOW, 1 point, to the player who captured the lowest-ranked trump played (this may be the same card as High). GAME, 1 point, to the player whose captured pile has the most card points; if two or more players tie for most, nobody scores Game. THREE, 3 points, to the player who captured the trump of rank 3; if it was not dealt, nobody scores it. Each player's deal points are the sum of the categories they won, from 0 to 6. Otherwise the pitcher is SET: the pitcher subtracts the contract from their score and does not add their deal points. Scores may go negative. Captured piles are then cleared and the next deal begins.

COMMUNICATION: There is no table talk. Players communicate only through bids and played cards.

END: After the 9th deal is scored, the game ends. The highest total score wins; players tied for the highest total share the result (a draw).

DECK: 24 cards in three suits (Red, Blue, Green), each with ranks 1 to 8. Cards are shown as codes suit*10+rank (Red=1, Blue=2, Green=3), so 18 is Red 8 and 23 is Blue 3. Card points, used only for Game: rank 8 = 4, rank 7 = 3, rank 6 = 2, rank 5 = 1, all other ranks = 0.

BID: Everyone answers at the same moment with one answer of two parts: PASS or a whole number from 2 to 6, and one suit that is in your own hand. A suit must be named even when passing (for example '4 Blue' or 'PASS Red'). Every player's amount (or PASS) is then revealed. The highest number wins: that player becomes the pitcher, the number becomes the contract and their named suit becomes trump. A tie goes to the tied player who comes first in priority order. The pitcher, contract and trump are announced; the suits named by the other two players are never revealed.

TRICKS: Three cards are played one at a time, starting with the leader and continuing in seat order. In the first trick of a deal the pitcher leads and must lead a trump (they always hold one). In later tricks the winner of the previous trick leads any card. Each later player must play a card of the led suit if they hold one, but may instead play a trump even if they hold the led suit; a player holding no card of the led suit may play any card. Captured piles are then cleared and the next deal begins.

COMMUNICATION: There is no table talk. Players communicate only through bids and played cards.

END: After the 9th deal is scored, the game ends. The highest total score wins; players tied for the highest total share the result (a draw).

=== Pocket Smear ===

Pocket Smear is for exactly 3 players, seated as Player 1, Player 2 and Player 3. Seat order is 1, 2, 3, then back to 1.

DECK: 24 cards in three suits (Red, Blue, Green), each with ranks 1 to 8. Cards are shown as codes suit*10+rank (Red=1, Blue=2, Green=3), so 18 is Red 8 and 23 is Blue 3. Card points, used only for Game: rank 8 = 4, rank 7 = 3, rank 6 = 2, rank 5 = 1, all other ranks = 0.

STRUCTURE: The game is 9 deals of 4 tricks each, one trick per round (36 rounds). Player 1 deals deals 1, 4 and 7; Player 2 deals 2, 5 and 8; Player 3 deals 3, 6 and 9. Priority order for a deal is: the player after the dealer, then the next player, then the dealer. All scores start at 0.

DEAL: All 24 cards are shuffled and each player is dealt 4 private cards. The other 12 are set aside face down, unseen by anyone, for the whole deal. You see only your own hand.

BID: Everyone answers at the same moment with one answer of two parts: PASS or a whole number from 2 to 6, and one suit that is in your own hand. A suit must be named even when passing (for example '4 Blue' or 'PASS Red'). Every player's amount (or PASS) is then revealed. The highest number wins: that player becomes the pitcher, the number becomes the contract and their named suit becomes trump. A tie goes to the tied player who comes first in priority order. If all three pass, the dealer becomes the pitcher with contract 2, and trump is the suit the dealer named. The pitcher, contract and trump are announced; the suits named by the other two players are never revealed.

TRICKS: Three cards are played one at a time, starting with the leader and continuing in seat order. In the first trick of a deal the pitcher leads and must lead a trump (they always hold one). In later tricks the winner of the previous trick leads any card. Each later player must play a card of the led suit if they hold one, but may instead play a trump even if they hold the led suit; a player holding no card of the led suit may play any card. You are only offered legal cards. The trick goes to the highest-ranked trump played; if no trump was played, it goes to the highest-ranked card of the led suit. Each of the two non-pitchers adds their deal points to their score. If the pitcher's deal points are at least the contract, the pitcher adds their deal points to their score. Otherwise the pitcher is SET: the pitcher subtracts the contract from their score and does not add their deal points. Scores may go negative. Captured piles are then cleared and the next deal begins.

COMMUNICATION: There is no table talk. Players communicate only through bids and played cards.

END: After the 9th deal is scored, the game ends. The highest total score wins; players tied for the highest total share the result (a draw).

[user]
=== Pocket Smear ===

Pocket Smear is for exactly 3 players, seated as Player 1, Player 2 and Player 3. Seat order is 1, 2, 3, then back to 1.

DECK: 24 cards in three suits (Red, Blue, Green), each with ranks 1 to 8. Cards are shown as codes suit*10+rank (Red=1, Blue=2, Green=3), so 18 is Red 8 and 23 is Blue 3. Card points, used only for Game: rank 8 = 4, rank 7 = 3, rank 6 = 2, rank 5 = 1, all other ranks = 0.

STRUCTURE: The game is 9 deals of 4 tricks each, one trick per round (36 rounds). Player 1 deals deals 1, 4 and 7; Player 2 deals 2, 5 and 8; Player 3 deals 3, 6 and 9. Priority order for a deal is: the player after the dealer, then the next player, then the dealer. All scores start at 0.

DEAL: All 24 cards are shuffled and each player is dealt 4 private cards. The other 12 are set aside face down, unseen by anyone, for the whole deal. You see only your own hand.

BID: Everyone answers at the same moment with one answer of two parts: PASS or a whole number from 2 to 6, and one suit that is in your own hand. A suit must be named even when passing (for example '4 Blue' or 'PASS Red'). Every player's amount (or PASS) is then revealed. The highest number wins: that player becomes the pitcher, the number becomes the contract and their named suit becomes trump. A tie goes to the tied player who comes first in priority order. If all three pass, the dealer becomes the pitcher with contract 2, and trump is the suit the dealer named. The pitcher, contract and trump are announced; the suits named by the other two players are never revealed.

TRICKS: Three cards are played one at a time, starting with the leader and continuing in seat order. In the first trick of a deal the pitcher leads and must lead a trump (they always hold one). In later tricks the winner of the previous trick leads any card. Each later player must play a card of the led suit if they hold one, but may instead play a trump even if they hold the led suit; a player holding no card of the led suit may play any card. You are only offered legal cards. The trick goes to the highest-ranked trump played; if no trump was played, it goes to the highest-ranked card of the led suit. All played cards are visible to everyone, and the three cards go into the trick winner's captured pile.

DEAL SCORING (after the 4th trick; only cards played this deal count): HIGH, 1 point, to the player who captured the highest-ranked trump played. LOW, 1 point, to the player who captured the lowest-ranked trump played (this may be the same card as High). GAME, 1 point, to the player whose captured pile has the most card points; if two or more players tie for most, nobody scores Game. THREE, 3 points, to the player who captured the trump of rank 3; if it was not dealt, nobody scores it. Each player's deal points are the sum of the categories they won, from 0 to 6. Each of the two non-pitchers adds their deal points to their score. If the pitcher's deal points are at least the contract, the pitcher adds their deal points to their score. Otherwise the pitcher is SET: the pitcher subtracts the contract from their score and does not add their deal points. Scores may go negative. Captured piles are then cleared and the next deal begins.

COMMUNICATION: There is no table talk. Players communicate only through bids and played cards.

END: After the 9th deal is scored, the game ends. The highest total score wins; players tied for the highest total share the result (a draw).

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 3. Seats are numbered 1 to 3.
You are seat 2, Blaise. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

Players 1, 2 and 3 take their seats. Play passes 1, 2, 3, then back to 1. All scores start at 0.

Each round runs in this order: the deal → your hand → the bid → the bid resolves → the bids revealed → the pitcher → lead options → the lead → follow options → second card → third card → the trick resolves → the deal is scored → deal results → advance → after the last deal.

=== Pocket Smear ===

Pocket Smear is for exactly 3 players, seated as Player 1, Player 2 and Player 3. Seat order is 1, 2, 3, then back to 1.

DECK: 24 cards in three suits (Red, Blue, Green), each with ranks 1 to 8. Cards are shown as codes suit*10+rank (Red=1, Blue=2, Green=3), so 18 is Red 8 and 23 is Blue 3. Card points, used only for Game: rank 8 = 4, rank 7 = 3, rank 6 = 2, rank 5 = 1, all other ranks = 0.

STRUCTURE: The game is 9 deals of 4 tricks each, one trick per round (36 rounds). Player 1 deals deals 1, 4 and 7; Player 2 deals 2, 5 and 8; Player 3 deals 3, 6 and 9. Priority order for a deal is: the player after the dealer, then the next player, then the dealer. All scores start at 0.

DEAL: All 24 cards are shuffled and each player is dealt 4 private cards. The other 12 are set aside face down, unseen by anyone, for the whole deal. You see only your own hand.

BID: Everyone answers at the same moment with one answer of two parts: PASS or a whole number from 2 to 6, and one suit that is in your own hand. A suit must be named even when passing (for example '4 Blue' or 'PASS Red'). Every player's amount (or PASS) is then revealed. The highest number wins: that player becomes the pitcher, the number becomes the contract and their named suit becomes trump. A tie goes to the tied player who comes first in priority order. If all three pass, the dealer becomes the pitcher with contract 2, and trump is the suit the dealer named. The pitcher, contract and trump are announced; the suits named by the other two players are never revealed.

TRICKS: Three cards are played one at a time, starting with the leader and continuing in seat order. In the first trick of a deal the pitcher leads and must lead a trump (they always hold one). In later tricks the winner of the previous trick leads any card. Each later player must play a card of the led suit if they hold one, but may instead play a trump even if they hold the led suit; a player holding no card of the led suit may play any card. You are only offered legal cards. The trick goes to the highest-ranked trump played; if no trump was played, it goes to the highest-ranked card of the led suit. Captured piles are then cleared and the next deal begins.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Pocket Smear ===

Pocket Smear is for exactly 3 players, seated as Player 1, Player 2 and Player 3. Seat order is 1, 2, 3, then back to 1.

DECK: 24 cards in three suits (Red, Blue, Green), each with ranks 1 to 8. Cards are shown as codes suit*10+rank (Red=1, Blue=2, Green=3), so 18 is Red 8 and 23 is Blue 3. Card points, used only for Game: rank 8 = 4, rank 7 = 3, rank 6 = 2, rank 5 = 1, all other ranks = 0.

STRUCTURE: The game is 9 deals of 4 tricks each, one trick per round (36 rounds). Player 1 deals deals 1, 4 and 7; Player 2 deals 2, 5 and 8; Player 3 deals 3, 6 and 9. Priority order for a deal is: the player after the dealer, then the next player, then the dealer. All scores start at 0.

DEAL: All 24 cards are shuffled and each player is dealt 4 private cards. The other 12 are set aside face down, unseen by anyone, for the whole deal. You see only your own hand.

BID: Everyone answers at the same moment with one answer of two parts: PASS or a whole number from 2 to 6, and one suit that is in your own hand. A suit must be named even when passing (for example '4 Blue' or 'PASS Red'). Every player's amount (or PASS) is then revealed. The highest number wins: that player becomes the pitcher, the number becomes the contract and their named suit becomes trump. A tie goes to the tied player who comes first in priority order. If all three pass, the dealer becomes the pitcher with contract 2, and trump is the suit the dealer named. The pitcher, contract and trump are announced; the suits named by the other two players are never revealed.

TRICKS: Three cards are played one at a time, starting with the leader and continuing in seat order. In the first trick of a deal the pitcher leads and must lead a trump (they always hold one). In later tricks the winner of the previous trick leads any card. Each later player must play a card of the led suit if they hold one, but may instead play a trump even if they hold the led suit; a player holding no card of the led suit may play any card. You are only offered legal cards. The trick goes to the highest-ranked trump played; if no trump was played, it goes to the highest-ranked card of the led suit. All played cards are visible to everyone, and the three cards go into the trick winner's captured pile.

DEAL SCORING (after the 4th trick; only cards played this deal count): HIGH, 1 point, to the player who captured the highest-ranked trump played. LOW, 1 point, to the player who captured the lowest-ranked trump played (this may be the same card as High). GAME, 1 point, to the player whose captured pile has the most card points; if two or more players tie for most, nobody scores Game. THREE, 3 points, to the player who captured the trump of rank 3; if it was not dealt, nobody scores it. Each player's deal points are the sum of the categories they won, from 0 to 6. Each of the two non-pitchers adds their deal points to their score. If the pitcher's deal points are at least the contract, the pitcher adds their deal points to their score. Otherwise the pitcher is SET: the pitcher subtracts the contract from their score and does not add their deal points. Scores may go negative. Pocket Smear is for exactly 3 players, seated as Player 1, Player 2 and Player 3. Seat order is 1, 2, 3, then back to 1.

STRUCTURE: The game is 9 deals of 4 tricks each, one trick per round (36 rounds). Player 1 deals deals 1, 4 and 7; Player 2 deals 2, 5 and 8; Player 3 deals 3, 6 and 9. Priority order for a deal is: the player after the dealer, then the next player, then the dealer. All scores start at 0.

DEAL: All 24 cards are shuffled and each player is dealt 4 private cards. The other 12 are set aside face down, unseen by anyone, for the whole deal. You see only your own hand.

BID: Everyone answers at the same moment with one answer of two parts: PASS or a whole number from 2 to 6, and one suit that is in your own hand. A suit must be named even when passing (for example '4 Blue' or 'PASS Red'). Every player's amount (or PASS) is then revealed. The highest number wins: that player becomes the pitcher, the number becomes the contract and their named suit becomes trump. A tie goes to the tied player who comes first in priority order. If all three pass, the dealer becomes the pitcher with contract 2, and trump is the suit the dealer named. The pitcher, contract and trump are announced; the suits named by the other two players are never revealed.

TRICKS: Three cards are played one at a time, starting with the leader and continuing in seat order. In the first trick of a deal the pitcher leads and must lead a trump (they always hold one). Each later player must play a card of the led suit if they hold one, but may instead play a trump even if they hold the led suit; a player holding no card of the led suit may play any card. Each of the two non-pitchers adds their deal points to their score. If the pitcher's deal points are at least the contract, the pitcher adds their deal points to their score. Otherwise the pitcher is SET: the pitcher subtracts the contract from their score and does not add their deal points. Scores may go negative. Captured piles are then cleared and the next deal begins.

Pocket Smear is for exactly 3 players, seated as Player 1, Player 2 and Player 3. Seat order is 1, 2, 3, then back to 1.

STRUCTURE: The game is 9 deals of 4 tricks each, one trick per round (36 rounds). Player 1 deals deals 1, 4 and 7; Player 2 deals 2, 5 and 8; Player 3 deals 3, 6 and 9. Priority order for a deal is: the player after the dealer, then the next player, then the dealer. All scores start at 0.

DEAL: All 24 cards are shuffled and each player is dealt 4 private cards. The other 12 are set aside face down, unseen by anyone, for the whole deal. You see only your own hand.

BID: Everyone answers at the same moment with one answer of two parts: PASS or a whole number from 2 to 6, and one suit that is in your own hand. A suit must be named even when passing (for example '4 Blue' or 'PASS Red'). Every player's amount (or PASS) is then revealed. The highest number wins: that player becomes the pitcher, the number becomes the contract and their named suit becomes trump. A tie goes to the tied player who comes first in priority order. If all three pass, the dealer becomes the pitcher with contract 2, and trump is the suit the dealer named. The pitcher, contract and trump are announced; the suits named by the other two players are never revealed.

TRICKS: Three cards are played one at a time, starting with the leader and continuing in seat order. In the first trick of a deal the pitcher leads and must lead a trump (they always hold one). In later tricks the winner of the previous trick leads any card. Each later player must play a card of the led suit if they hold one, but may instead play a trump even if they hold the led suit; a player holding no card of the led suit may play any card. You are only offered legal cards. The trick goes to the highest-ranked trump played; if no trump was played, it goes to the highest-ranked card of the led suit. All played cards are visible to everyone, and the three cards go into the trick winner's captured pile.

Otherwise the pitcher is SET: the pitcher subtracts the contract from their score and does not add their deal points. Scores may go negative. Captured piles are then cleared and the next deal begins.

COMMUNICATION: There is no table talk. Players communicate only through bids and played cards.

END: After the 9th deal is scored, the game ends. The highest total score wins; players tied for the highest total share the result (a draw).

Think about the rules, the other players and what they have done, then act. When you are asked to act, reply with exactly one legal answer in the form the question asks for, and keep any reasoning short and before the answer. Do not ask questions back.

[user]
=== Pocket Smear ===

Pocket Smear is for exactly 3 players, seated as Player 1, Player 2 and Player 3. Seat order is 1, 2, 3, then back to 1.

DECK: 24 cards in three suits (Red, Blue, Green), each with ranks 1 to 8. Cards are shown as codes suit*10+rank (Red=1, Blue=2, Green=3), so 18 is Red 8 and 23 is Blue 3. Card points, used only for Game: rank 8 = 4, rank 7 = 3, rank 6 = 2, rank 5 = 1, all other ranks = 0.

STRUCTURE: The game is 9 deals of 4 tricks each, one trick per round (36 rounds). Player 1 deals deals 1, 4 and 7; Player 2 deals 2, 5 and 8; Player 3 deals 3, 6 and 9. Priority order for a deal is: the player after the dealer, then the next player, then the dealer. All scores start at 0.

DEAL: All 24 cards are shuffled and each player is dealt 4 private cards. The other 12 are set aside face down, unseen by anyone, for the whole deal. You see only your own hand.

BID: Everyone answers at the same moment with one answer of two parts: PASS or a whole number from 2 to 6, and one suit that is in your own hand. A suit must be named even when passing (for example '4 Blue' or 'PASS Red'). Every player's amount (or PASS) is then revealed. The highest number wins: that player becomes the pitcher, the number becomes the contract and their named suit becomes trump. A tie goes to the tied player who comes first in priority order. If all three pass, the dealer becomes the pitcher with contract 2, and trump is the suit the dealer named. The pitcher, contract and trump are announced; the suits named by the other two players are never revealed.

TRICKS: Three cards are played one at a time, starting with the leader and continuing in seat order. In the first trick of a deal the pitcher leads and must lead a trump (they always hold one). In later tricks the winner of the previous trick leads any card. Each later player must play a card of the led suit if they hold one, but may instead play a trump even if they hold the led suit; a player holding no card of the led suit may play any card. You are only offered legal cards. The trick goes to the highest-ranked trump played; if no trump was played, it goes to the highest-ranked card of the led suit. All played cards are visible to everyone, and the three cards go into the trick winner's captured pile.

DEAL SCORING (after the 4th trick; only cards played this deal count): HIGH, 1 point, to the player who captured the highest-ranked trump played. LOW, 1 point, to the player who captured the lowest-ranked trump played (this may be the same card as High). GAME, 1 point, to the player whose captured pile has the most card points; if two or more players tie for most, nobody scores Game. THREE, 3 points, to the player who captured the trump of rank 3; if it was not dealt, nobody scores it. Each player's deal points are the sum of the categories they won, from 0 to 6. Each of the two non-pitchers adds their deal points to their score. If the pitcher's deal points are at least the contract, the pitcher adds their deal points to their score. Otherwise the pitcher is SET: the pitcher subtracts the contract from their score and does not add their deal points. Scores may go negative. Captured piles are then cleared and the next deal begins.

COMMUNICATION: There is no table talk. Players communicate only through bids and played cards.

END: After the 9th deal is scored, the game ends. The highest total score wins; players tied for the highest total share the result (a draw).

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 3. Seats are numbered 1 to 3.
You are seat 2, Blaise. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

Players 1, 2 and 3 take their seats. Play passes 1, 2, 3, then back to 1. All scores start at 0.

Each round runs in this order: the deal → your hand → the bid → the bid resolves → the bids revealed → the pitcher → lead options → the lead → follow options → second card → third card → the trick resolves → the deal is scored → deal results → advance → after the last deal.

  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,

  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

=== Pocket Smear ===

Pocket Smear is for exactly 3 players, seated as Player 1, Player 2 and Player 3. Seat order is 1, 2, 3, then back to 1.

DECK: 24 cards in three suits (Red, Blue, Green), each with ranks 1 to 8. Cards are shown as codes suit*10+rank (Red=1, Blue=2, Green=3), so 18 is Red 8 and 23 is Blue 3. Card points, used only for Game: rank 8 = 4, rank 7 = 3, rank 6 = 2, rank 5 = 1, all other ranks = 0.

STRUCTURE: The game is 9 deals of 4 tricks each, one trick per round (36 rounds). Player 1 deals deals 1, 4 and 7; Player 2 deals 2, 5 and 8; Player 3 deals 3, 6 and 9. Priority order for a deal is: the player after the dealer, then the next player, then the dealer. All scores start at 0.

DEAL: All 24 cards are shuffled and each player is dealt 4 private cards. The other 12 are set aside face down, unseen by anyone, for the whole deal. You see only your own hand.

BID: Everyone answers at the same moment with one answer of two parts: PASS or a whole number from 2 to 6, and one suit that is in your own hand. A suit must be named even when passing (for example '4 Blue' or 'PASS Red'). Every player's amount (or PASS) is then revealed. The highest number wins: that player becomes the pitcher, the number becomes the contract and their named suit becomes trump. A tie goes to the tied player who comes first in priority order. If all three pass, the dealer becomes the pitcher with contract 2, and trump is the suit the dealer named. The pitcher, contract and trump are announced; the suits named by the other two players are never revealed.

TRICKS: Three cards are played one at a time, starting with the leader and continuing in seat order. In the first trick of a deal the pitcher leads and must lead a trump (they always hold one). In later tricks the winner of the previous trick leads any card. Each later player must play a card of the led suit if they hold one, but may instead play a trump even if they hold the led suit; a player holding no card of the led suit may play any card. You are only offered legal cards. The trick goes to the highest-ranked trump played; if no trump was played, it goes to the highest-ranked card of the led suit. All played cards are visible to everyone, and the three cards go into the trick winner's captured pile.

DEAL SCORING (after the 4th trick; only cards played this deal count): HIGH, 1 point, to the player who captured the highest-ranked trump played. LOW, 1 point, to the player who captured the lowest-ranked trump played (this may be the same card as High). GAME, 1 point, to the player whose captured pile has the most card points; if two or more players tie for most, nobody scores Game. THREE, 3 points, to the player who captured the trump of rank 3; if it was not dealt, nobody scores it. Each player's deal points are the sum of the categories they won, from 0 to 6. Each of the two non-pitchers adds their deal points to their score. If the pitcher's deal points are at least the contract, the pitcher adds their deal points to their score. Otherwise the pitcher is SET: the pitcher subtracts the contract from their score and does not add their deal points. Scores may go negative. Captured piles are then cleared and the next deal begins.

COMMUNICATION: There is no table talk. Players communicate only through bids and played cards.

END: After the 9th deal is scored, the game ends. The highest total score wins; players tied for the highest total share the result (a draw).

Pocket Smear is for exactly 3 players, seated as Player 1, Player 2 and Player 3. Seat order is 1, 2, 3, then back to 1.

DECK: 24 cards in three suits (Red, Blue, Green), each with ranks 1 to 8. Cards are shown as codes suit*10+rank (Red=1, Blue=2, Green=3), so 18 is Red 8 and 23 is Blue 3. Card points, used only for Game: rank 8 = 4, rank 7 = 3, rank 6 = 2, rank 5 = 1, all other ranks = 0.

STRUCTURE: The game is 9 deals of 4 tricks each, one trick per round (36 rounds). Player 1 deals deals 1, 4 and 7; Player 2 deals 2, 5 and 8; Player 3 deals 3, 6 and 9. Priority order for a deal is: the player after the dealer, then the next player, then the dealer. All scores start at 0.

DEAL: All 24 cards are shuffled and each player is dealt 4 private cards. The other 12 are set aside face down, unseen by anyone, for the whole deal. You see only your own hand.

BID: Everyone answers at the same moment with one answer of two parts: PASS or a whole number from 2 to 6, and one suit that is in your own hand. A suit must be named even when passing (for example '4 Blue' or 'PASS Red'). Every player's amount (or PASS) is then revealed. The highest number wins: that player becomes the pitcher, the number becomes the contract and their named suit becomes trump. A tie goes to the tied player who comes first in priority order. If all three pass, the dealer becomes the pitcher with contract 2, and trump is the suit the dealer named. The pitcher, contract and trump are announced; the suits named by the other two players are never revealed.

In later tricks the winner of the previous trick leads any card. Each later player must play a card of the led suit if they hold one, but may instead play a trump even if they hold the led suit; a player holding no card of the led suit may play any card. DECK: 24 cards in three suits (Red, Blue, Green), each with ranks 1 to 8. Cards are shown as codes suit*10+rank (Red=1, Blue=2, Green=3), so 18 is Red 8 and 23 is Blue 3. Card points, used only for Game: rank 8 = 4, rank 7 = 3, rank 6 = 2, rank 5 = 1, all other ranks = 0.

STRUCTURE: The game is 9 deals of 4 tricks each, one trick per round (36 rounds). Player 1 deals deals 1, 4 and 7; Player 2 deals 2, 5 and 8; Player 3 deals 3, 6 and 9. Priority order for a deal is: the player after the dealer, then the next player, then the dealer. All scores start at 0.

DEAL: All 24 cards are shuffled and each player is dealt 4 private cards. The other 12 are set aside face down, unseen by anyone, for the whole deal. You see only your own hand.

BID: Everyone answers at the same moment with one answer of two parts: PASS or a whole number from 2 to 6, and one suit that is in your own hand. A suit must be named even when passing (for example '4 Blue' or 'PASS Red'). Every player's amount (or PASS) is then revealed. The highest number wins: that player becomes the pitcher, the number becomes the contract and their named suit becomes trump. A tie goes to the tied player who comes first in priority order. If all three pass, the dealer becomes the pitcher with contract 2, and trump is the suit the dealer named. The pitcher, contract and trump are announced; the suits named by the other two players are never revealed.

TRICKS: Three cards are played one at a time, starting with the leader and continuing in seat order. In the first trick of a deal the pitcher leads and must lead a trump (they always hold one). In later tricks the winner of the previous trick leads any card. Each later player must play a card of the led suit if they hold one, but may instead play a trump even if they hold the led suit; a player holding no card of the led suit may play any card. You are only offered legal cards. The trick goes to the highest-ranked trump played; if no trump was played, it goes to the highest-ranked card of the led suit. All played cards are visible to everyone, and the three cards go into the trick winner's captured pile.

DEAL SCORING (after the 4th trick; only cards played this deal count): HIGH, 1 point, to the player who captured the highest-ranked trump played. LOW, 1 point, to the player who captured the lowest-ranked trump played (this may be the same card as High). GAME, 1 point, to the player whose captured pile has the most card points; if two or more players tie for most, nobody scores Game. THREE, 3 points, to the player who captured the trump of rank 3; if it was not dealt, nobody scores it. Each player's deal points are the sum of the categories they won, from 0 to 6. Each of the two non-pitchers adds their deal points to their score. If the pitcher's deal points are at least the contract, the pitcher adds their deal points to their score. Otherwise the pitcher is SET: the pitcher subtracts the contract from their score and does not add their deal points. Scores may go negative. Captured piles are then cleared and the next deal begins.

COMMUNICATION: There is no table talk. Players communicate only through bids and played cards.

END: After the 9th deal is scored, the game ends. The highest total score wins; players tied for the highest total share the result (a draw).

records.system:
You are reviewing a game that has finished. You were not a player. You are shown everything: the messages the table was told, every move, and each player's private thinking at every move, which no other player ever saw. Each move carries the notes its game asked for, under their own names. The usual ones are:

  plan     what they meant to do over the coming turns
  reason   why they made that move
  predict  what they expected their opponents to do
  adjust   how they changed their own strategy because of that

Write two things.

First, a summary of the whole game as it unfolded: the turning points, the moves that decided it, and how it ended. Concrete: name seats, rounds and numbers.

Second, a review of each player. Judge their play, not their luck. For each one, compare their predictions with what their opponents were actually thinking and actually did: were they right, and did they see it in time? Did their adjustments follow from their predictions, and did their moves follow from their reasons? Point out their best and worst moves. Then score their play from 1 to 10, where 1 is aimless or self-defeating and 10 is sharp, well read and well executed. A player can lose and still score well, or win and score badly.

A player who gave no reasons, predictions or adjustments is judged on their moves alone; say that their thinking was not recorded.

Refer to each player by seat, and as "they".

THE GAME
Pocket Smear is for exactly 3 players, seated as Player 1, Player 2 and Player 3. Seat order is 1, 2, 3, then back to 1.

DECK: 24 cards in three suits (Red, Blue, Green), each with ranks 1 to 8. Cards are shown as codes suit*10+rank (Red=1, Blue=2, Green=3), so 18 is Red 8 and 23 is Blue 3. Card points, used only for Game: rank 8 = 4, rank 7 = 3, rank 6 = 2, rank 5 = 1, all other ranks = 0.

STRUCTURE: The game is 9 deals of 4 tricks each, one trick per round (36 rounds). Player 1 deals deals 1, 4 and 7; Player 2 deals 2, 5 and 8; Player 3 deals 3, 6 and 9. Priority order for a deal is: the player after the dealer, then the next player, then the dealer. All scores start at 0.

DEAL: All 24 cards are shuffled and each player is dealt 4 private cards. The other 12 are set aside face down, unseen by anyone, for the whole deal. You see only your own hand.

BID: Everyone answers at the same moment with one answer of two parts: PASS or a whole number from 2 to 6, and one suit that is in your own hand. A suit must be named even when passing (for example '4 Blue' or 'PASS Red'). Every player's amount (or PASS) is then revealed. The highest number wins: that player becomes the pitcher, the number becomes the contract and their named suit becomes trump. A tie goes to the tied player who comes first in priority order. If all three pass, the dealer becomes the pitcher with contract 2, and trump is the suit the dealer named. The pitcher, contract and trump are announced; the suits named by the other two players are never revealed.

TRICKS: Three cards are played one at a time, starting with the leader and continuing in seat order. In the first trick of a deal the pitcher leads and must lead a trump (they always hold one). In later tricks the winner of the previous trick leads any card. Each later player must play a card of the led suit if they hold one, but may instead play a trump even if they hold the led suit; a player holding no card of the led suit may play any card. You are only offered legal cards. The trick goes to the highest-ranked trump played; if no trump was played, it goes to the highest-ranked card of the led suit. All played cards are visible to everyone, and the three cards go into the trick winner's captured pile.

DEAL SCORING (after the 4th trick; only cards played this deal count): HIGH, 1 point, to the player who captured the highest-ranked trump played. LOW, 1 point, to the player who captured the lowest-ranked trump played (this may be the same card as High). GAME, 1 point, to the player whose captured pile has the most card points; if two or more players tie for most, nobody scores Game. THREE, 3 points, to the player who captured the trump of rank 3; if it was not dealt, nobody scores it. Each player's deal points are the sum of the categories they won, from 0 to 6. Each of the two non-pitchers adds their deal points to their score. If the pitcher's deal points are at least the contract, the pitcher adds their deal points to their score. Otherwise the pitcher is SET: the pitcher subtracts the contract from their score and does not add their deal points. Scores may go negative. Captured piles are then cleared and the next deal begins.

COMMUNICATION: There is no table talk. Players communicate only through bids and played cards.

END: After the 9th deal is scored, the game ends. The highest total score wins; players tied for the highest total share the result (a draw).
